jobs.name: woodland-borough-balanced-v3
jobs.prompt:
Use case: compositing.
Asset type: screenshot paintover to test economical game-ready sci-fi building assets inside an EXISTING higher-fidelity engine environment.
INPUT IMAGE 1 IS THE ACTUAL GAME SCREENSHOT AND THE EDIT TARGET. INPUT IMAGE 2 is an older concept to guide ONLY the placement and broad design of buildings, NOT a style to copy onto the environment.
TOP PRIORITY: keep the natural environment of IMAGE 1 unchanged. The existing trees, their leaf shapes and textures, trunk shapes, grass blades, flowers, terrain texture, shadows, lighting, sky color, perspective and camera framing MUST remain as in image 1. Do not remake the landscape. Use it as the original background plate, occluding only small areas where new structures and the footpath belong. Remove the upper-left debug HUD and fill with matching sky and original tree context. Preserve the large foreground trunk just right of center, its branches and existing cast shadow exactly. Keep every foreground flower and grass patch wherever not occupied by the footpath. Absolutely no faceted tree crowns, polygon terrain patches, low-poly grass, cartoon sky or flat-shaded world.
Insert a small frontier service settlement matching the general layout in image 2: workshop under the left trees, clinic in the central background, residences between the right trees, water equipment at far right, and a modest worn path to the yard. Use ordinary adult scale and preserve the tree trunks IN FRONT OF structures. Buildings are an economical but convincing hard-surface game-art kit: simple chamfered prefabricated shells, clean smoothly shaded ivory/composite wall panels, teal doors and accent panels, charcoal metal support parts, small muted orange utility markings. Rounded edges have modest smooth bevels rather than exaggerated single flat chamfers. Tanks have smoothly shaded cylindrical walls with simple caps. Maintain physically grounded material response: subtle roughness variation, broad seams and believable ambient shading, with very restrained wear.
The earlier detailed concept had too many tiny fittings and surface details. Simplify THAT only: remove most little cables, bolts, loose tools, dense tiny panels, antennas and pipe tangles. Keep functional doors, dark inset windows, a handful of broad panel seams, one simple air vent per building, a thick structural canopy frame and a readable porch. Water equipment consists of two smooth-sided tanks, a few thick straight pipes with simple rounded elbows and a control cabinet. Canopies should have a believable shallow fabric sag and warm ochre color. One modest cargo buggy and three residents may indicate scale, with natural proportions and subdued workwear.
This should look like moderately detailed modular assets built and cleaned up in Blender, comfortably matching the original forest rendering. Simple construction and restrained detail, not a flat low-poly illustration, not toy-like, not photoreal prop scans covered in greebles. Do not adopt the newer faceted art style. Lighting must match the original screenshot. Preserve original image 1 camera and aspect ratio. Single complete scene; no comparison panels, captions, labels, UI, or watermark.
Repeat: the trees, foliage and ground of image 1 remain the CURRENT ENGINE LOOK. Only added man-made assets receive simpler modeling.
